# What ZINDO/S-CIS does to photoexcitation

Every number below is read out of `results.tsv`, which is written by
`cargo test --test photoexcitation`. Nothing here is transcribed by hand,
and nothing is compared against a literature value -- see **What this
study does not do**.

## The set

9 molecules, 54 singlet and 54 triplet roots: ethene, butadiene, benzene, pyridine, pyrazine, formaldehyde, glyoxal, acrolein, formamide.

Planar, C/N/O/H only, so every atom is inside the ZINDO/S s-p branch and
no result here is confounded by a missing parameter. The ring geometries
are regular polygons: the right idealisation for asking what the model
does with a state of a given symmetry, and the wrong one for comparing an
excitation energy with an experimental band maximum, which this study
does not do.

## Polarisation

Of 54 singlet roots, 20 are in-plane, 17 out-of-plane and 17 dark.

For a planar molecule this classification is exact rather than
approximate. Reflection in the molecular plane is a symmetry; pi orbitals
are odd under it and in-plane orbitals even, and of the dipole components
the two in-plane ones are even and the normal one odd. So a
parity-preserving excitation can only couple to the in-plane components
and a parity-changing one only to the normal component. A test asserts
that no root is polarised partly along both, and none is.

Two readings that the table refuses, both of which a looser classifier
would make:

* **dark is not n->pi\***. Benzene's two lowest singlets are dark and both
  are pi->pi\*; benzene has no lone pair at all.
* **out-of-plane is not n->pi\*** either. Sigma orbitals are even under the
  reflection just as lone pairs are, so sigma->pi\* is out-of-plane too.
  Ethene, with no lone pair, has such a root at 8.73 eV.

And the limit of the approach: formaldehyde's n->pi\* is A2 in C2v, which
spans no component of the dipole, so it is not out-of-plane polarised but
*completely* dark -- invisible to a measure built on the transition
dipole's direction. It is in the table at 3.187 eV, identifiable instead
by its 2.55 D difference dipole. That is why the table carries the
difference dipole beside the polarisation rather than instead of it.

## The singlet-triplet gap separates the two state types on its own

Nothing in the set-up sorts the molecules; this comes out of the
calculation. `S1 - T1` is twice the exchange integral over the hole and
particle orbitals, so it measures how much the two overlap -- large when
both live in the same pi system, small when the hole is a lone pair in the
molecular plane and the particle is a pi\* orbital perpendicular to it.

| S1 character | molecules | S1 - T1 / eV |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| hole and particle share the pi system | ethene, butadiene, benzene | 2.50 to 4.70 |
| hole in the molecular plane, particle perpendicular | pyridine, pyrazine, formaldehyde, glyoxal, acrolein, formamide | 0.40 to 1.82 |

The two ranges do not overlap: the smallest gap in the first group is
2.50 eV and the largest in the second is 1.82 eV.

## What this study does not do

It does not compare a single excitation energy against a measured or
high-level-computed one, so it says nothing about how accurate ZINDO/S-CIS
is. That was deliberate twice over.

The first reason is that the comparison needs reference data this
repository does not have. Transcribing a benchmark set from a paper is
real work with a real error rate, and the project's rule for reference
numbers -- two independently written parsers, both sides re-read and
compared -- exists because of it. Guessing at remembered values instead
would have produced a study-shaped object with no evidence in it.

The second is that an accuracy number, on its own, would not have
separated the two errors that make it up: the CIS ansatz's, and the
semiempirical Hamiltonian's. Separating them needs a correlated method on
the same Hamiltonian, and post-HF is out of scope for v0.3.0. The natural
next step for this study is that decomposition, not a longer table.

What is here instead is a set of measurements against things that are
known exactly -- an asymptotic form, a reflection symmetry, a variational
bound. Those need no external data and admit no tolerance argument.
